args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of v2.3.1, checkout-api began failing health checks in every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, so the rollback didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovered metrics, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's deployed again. No other incidents were open beforehand.

The test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging before it went to production, which may be worth looking into.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0. Rolling back.
